interface.name: df_toplevel_manager

description.summary: window/workspace/output control for trusted clients

interface.description: The manager is per-client. On bind the compositor replays the current scene: it announces every output, workspace, and toplevel, then emits `done`. Binding requires a successful `df_core.authenticate`.

request.name: create_workspace

description.summary: create an empty Space at the end of every output

request.description: The new Space is announced with a `workspace` event and `done`.

description.summary: Mission Control selection: focus this window's Space and raise it
app switcher: activate the most recent window of an app
app switcher: move the selection by one app

request.name: release_keyboard_focus

description.summary: release chrome keyboard focus back to the active window

request.description: The shell calls this when keyboard focus leaves a chrome surface (T-10: Escape exits Dock keyboard navigation) so the compositor can restore the active window's focus. Inert when the active window is gone or no chrome surface held the keyboard.

request.name: set_reduced_motion

description.summary: set the compositor's reduced-motion policy

request.description: The shell mirrors `accessibility.reduceMotion` here so every compositor-driven transition (workspace slide, Mission Control open/ close, Desktop Reveal) takes the single-step path while still applying the same commit rule (T-11 FR-9). Additive in v3.

request.name: set_launch_origin

description.summary: set the Dock tile an app's windows appear from and minimize into

request.description: The shell sends the Dock entry's tile rectangle (logical global pixels) when it launches an app, so the compositor's window-appear transition scales and fades from the tile (T-02.1b) and minimize/ restore scale into and out of it (T-02.2). Keyed by `app_id` and remembered for the app's lifecycle motions; when the shell never sends one (headless, or a non-Dock launch) the compositor falls back to a centered origin. Additive in v4.

description.summary: one app in the switcher's recency snapshot

arg.name: index
arg.summary: position in recency order, 0 = most recent

request.name: set_motion_policy

description.summary: set the compositor's motion/appearance policy

request.description: The shell mirrors the settingsd motion keys here so the compositor's lifecycle motion, SSD titlebar behaviour, and drawn materials follow the one owner (T-08.2c). `color_scheme` is the resolved `light`/`dark` spelling (`appearance.colorScheme`; the shell resolves `auto` against the host), `titlebar_double_click` is `zoom`/`minimize`/`none` (`dock.titlebarDoubleClick`), and `minimized_animation` is `genie`/`scale`/`none` (`dock.minimizedAnimation`). Unknown spellings leave the current value untouched.

request.name: set_input_policy

description.summary: set keyboard repeat and gesture policy

request.description: The shell mirrors the settingsd input keys here (T-08.2c): `input.repeatDelay`/`input.repeatRate` (ms, Hz), `gestures.enabled`, `gestures.spaceSwitch`, and `gestures.missionControl`. The compositor applies them to the live seat and gesture recognizer immediately; no local settings file exists on either side.

request.name: capture_screenshot

description.summary: render and save a single-frame capture

request.description: The trusted shell asks the compositor for a screenshot of the active output, cropped to `x`,`y`,`width`,`height`, and writes it to a PNG at `path`. The compositor resolves the frame itself (no arbitrary grab protocol) and replies with `screenshot_saved` or `screenshot_failed`.

event.name: screenshot_saved

description.summary: a requested capture was rendered and written

event.description: Sent in reply to `capture_screenshot`; `path` is the file the compositor wrote the capture to. The path is the one the trusted shell supplied, never a new location. Additive in v6.

event.name: screenshot_failed

description.summary: a requested capture could not be produced

event.description: Sent in reply to `capture_screenshot` when the backend has no render target (headless), the selection is empty, or the frame could not be read back. `reason` is for logs only. Additive in v6.

request.name: set_app_accelerators

description.summary: replace the focused app's accelerator table

request.description: The shell mirrors the menu-broker's focus-scoped accelerator table here: one `action` per line, a tab, then the chord (`"quit\tSuper+Q"`). The compositor matches these only while `app_id` is focused and always lets its system shortcuts win; a matched chord is delivered back to the shell with `app_accelerator`. An empty table clears the app's accelerators. Malformed lines are skipped.

event.name: activation_result

description.summary: the compositor's answer to activate_app

event.description: Sent in reply to `activate_app`; `found` is 0 when the app had no window to activate. The shell falls back to a launch (when it knows the desktop id) or a notice, so a click never silently no-ops (T-14.7g).

request.name: set_appearance_policy

description.summary: set the effective scheme and glass preferences

request.description: The shell mirrors the settingsd appearance/accessibility keys here: `color_scheme` is the resolved `light`/`dark` spelling (the shell resolves `auto` against the host), `transparency_millionths` is the 0..1 attached-menu slider encoded as millionths (the schema's 0.5255 default is 525500), and the two overrides are `accessibility.reduceTransparency` / `accessibility.increaseContrast`. The compositor applies the whole snapshot atomically and repaints the material scene only when it changes. Unknown schemes leave the current scheme untouched; an out-of-range slider is clamped. The overrides are independent of the internal glass rollout switch.

request.name: set_pointer_policy

description.summary: set the live pointer/trackpad preferences

request.description: The shell mirrors the settingsd `input.*` pointer keys here. Speeds are millionths (-1000000..1000000, 0 neutral); the string fields use the schema's stable ids. Unknown spellings leave the current value untouched, and out-of-range speeds are clamped. The compositor applies the snapshot to its default pointer settings; per-device overrides remain the backend's.

request.name: set_keyboard_layout

description.summary: set the live keyboard layout

request.description: `layout` and `variant` are xkbcommon layout/variant names. A null layout keeps the host `XKB_DEFAULT_*` configuration. The compositor recompiles the seat keymap; an invalid layout is ignored and the current keymap stays in force.

interface.name: df_toplevel

description.summary: one managed window

interface.description: A server-created handle. The client never invents ids; it addresses windows by the compositor-stable id embedded in this object. The compositor emits initial properties followed by `done` right after the `toplevel` announcement.

description.summary: the window is gone; the handle is inert

interface.name: df_workspace

description.summary: one Space on one output

interface.description: Spaces are per-output and ordered; activation is lockstep across all outputs (03-workspaces.md). A fullscreen window owns a dedicated, transient Space; it reports `fullscreen` true.

description.summary: assign a wallpaper; NULL source keeps the solid color

interface.name: df_output

description.summary: one display

interface.description: Follows wlr-output-management: modes, scale, transform, plus VRR and night-light/color controls, brightness, and reserved zones. `set_*` requests are acknowledged with `done` after the backend applies them (or the compositor's best-effort equivalent).

description.summary: a shell surface reserved pixels on an edge; edge 0=top,1=bottom,2=left,3=right

request.name: set_brightness

description.summary: set the output's brightness level

request.description: The shell mirrors `display.brightness` here; the compositor owns the value and applies it best-effort. Additive in v2.

description.summary: the output's current brightness level
